nodes.title: Bounded-width positive-height sectors

The width is R and the height is η; constants in theorems may depend on both. Interior and translated half-open angular strips are used when selecting logarithms.
hypotheses: n is finite; R≥0; η>0.
proofSteps: Take coordinatewise intersections of closed inequalities in the real coordinates of C^n.
Use the identity map for n=0; no coordinate condition remains.

acceptance: In dimension one 0+2i lies in the width-one height-one sector, while 2+2i does not.

nodes.title: Definability of the lifted period map
nodes.statement: For an integral polarized pure VHS with unipotent coordinate monodromies on a polydisc neighbourhood, let Φ̃(z)=exp(Σz_iN_i)Ψ(q(z)) be its H.6 nilpotent-orbit lift into its H.3 semialgebraic period domain D. For every fixed R≥0 and η>0 for which the closed q-polydisc of radius exp(−2πη) is contained in the extension neighbourhood, Φ̃ restricted to boundedSector(n,R,η) is R_an,exp-definable. The neighbourhood condition cannot be replaced by holomorphy on the open unit polydisc alone.
hypotheses: H.2 integral polarized pure VHS; H.6 unipotent commuting N_i and holomorphic extension Ψ.
H.3 algebraic compact dual, algebraic group action, and semialgebraic D.
A compact q-buffer lies inside the extension domain.
proofSteps: Use sector-uniformization and the LD.6 bounded-strip exponential theorem.
Cover the compact q-buffer by finitely many algebraic compact-dual charts; Ψ is restricted analytic in these charts.
Commuting nilpotent logarithms have polynomial exponential, and the group action is algebraic; compose definable maps.

nodes.title: The varying Hodge form
nodes.statement: On a fixed complexification V_C of a free integral local system, with a family of pure Hodge structures hs_z and polarizations P_z supplied by H.2/H.3, hodgeFormFunction(P,z,u,v) is the conjugate of P_z.hodgeForm(u,v). Equivalently it is Q_C(C_z u,conjugate v), the BKT convention, linear in u and conjugate-linear in v. Its diagonal equals the native diagonal and is positive for u≠0. On real vectors it induces a real positive definite symmetric form b_z; this real restriction is what reduction theory uses.
hypotheses: Fixed lattice-induced conjugation and fixed weight k.
Polarization Q is flat in the chosen local trivialization.
proofSteps: Use the existing fibrewise Polarization.hodgeForm, not a new polarization definition.
Conjugate its value and apply hodgeForm_eq_conj.
Restrict to real points; conjugation fixes those vectors and Hermitian symmetry becomes real symmetry.

hypotheses: Finite dimensional V_C; H.6 distributive simultaneous splitting; choose homogeneous bases in each summand.
proofSteps: Choose bases in the finitely many nonzero splitting summands and order them by decreasing p.
Take native spans of the initial segments. Linear independence gives dimension j.
The splitting’s filtration identity gives the refinement of F.

nodes.title: Indefinite Gram determinants and Hodge entries
nodes.statement: Let w be hodge-adapted-flag at F=Ψ(0), γ(z)=exp(Σz_iN_i)exp(v(q(z))) the H.6 negative-Lie-chart lift, and B(u,v)=Q_C(u,conjugate v). Put W_j=w₁∧⋯∧w_j, Δ_j=B(γW_j,γW_j), Δ₀=1. Each Δ_j is nonzero wherever γF is pure. B-Gram–Schmidt vectors w̃_j satisfy B(w̃_j,w̃_j)=Δ_j/Δ_{j−1}; the j-th Hodge-entry contribution is i^{2p_j−k} B(γW_{j−1}∧u,γW_j) B(γW_j,γW_{j−1}∧v)/(Δ_{j−1}Δ_j). Summing gives h_z(u,v). For γu replace u by γu inside these exterior expressions. In odd weight B is skew-Hermitian; i^k B is Hermitian. The unit phases cancel correctly, and no positivity of B itself is asserted.
hypotheses: Polarization has weight parity Q(v,u)=(−1)^kQ(u,v).
The full flag refines the pure Hodge filtration after applying γ; nonvanishing uses its definite successive Hodge blocks.
proofSteps: Use the flag’s sorted p indices to identify orthogonal Hodge blocks and show that their leading Gram minors cannot vanish.
Apply Gram determinant identities to the Hermitian form i^kB and then undo the phase.
Use h=i^{2p_j−k}B on each pure component and sum the orthogonal contributions.

The nilpotent exponential is polynomial and the holomorphic big-cell correction is restricted analytic on a buffer, so the displayed numerators and minors lie in the coefficient Laurent-polynomial algebra.

sources.match: Notation Δ is introduced here for the source’s exterior B-values; phases and complex conjugation are retained.

acceptance: For a single pure Tate line, Δ₁=Q(w,conjugate w) and the phase produces its positive Hodge norm.
An arbitrary full flag, unrelated to the Hodge filtration, can have an isotropic first vector; no nonvanishing theorem is given for it.

nodes.title: Rough monomiality of flat multigraded Hodge norms
nodes.statement: For every nonzero vector u in one summand of either the H.6 simultaneous complex splitting I or any compatible rational weight splitting J, its flat squared norm h_z(u,u) belongs to the LD.6 rough-monomial class on a sufficiently deep orderedSector(n,R,Y). For weight labels σ=(σ₁,…,σₙ) the comparison monomial is m_σ(y)=(y₁/y₂)^{σ₁}⋯(y_{n−1}/yₙ)^{σ_{n−1}}yₙ^{σₙ}. Constants and Y depend on the fixed data, R and u; the two-sided estimate is not asserted for u=0. The same assertion holds in every exterior power with its induced polarized Hodge structure.
hypotheses: H.6 splitting-independent estimates for every compatible splitting, not just a chosen rational J.
LD.6 rough-monomial class means a rational coefficient-algebra function bounded above and below by positive multiples of a Laurent monomial.
proofSteps: Invoke H.6’s Kashiwara estimates to get the two-sided comparison with m_σ, including for complex I and determinant vectors.
Use gram-determinant-formulas to express the flat diagonal in the fraction algebra.
Combine fraction-algebra membership with the imported estimates; this node supplies rough-function membership, not a second proof of Kashiwara’s theorem.

sources.match: Separates fraction-algebra membership from the H.6 norm estimate.
The source estimates use compatible splittings and not a canonical rational-to-complex identification.

acceptance: For a constant Tate line, all centered weight labels are zero and the diagonal is constant.
The zero diagonal is not roughly monomial.

nodes.title: Rough monomiality of moving Hodge norms
nodes.statement: For nonzero homogeneous u in the simultaneous complex splitting and γ=exp(Σz_iN_i)exp(v(q)), h_z(γu,γu) is roughly monomial on a sufficiently deep ordered sector, including every exterior power. Its monomial is the one from the H.6 moving-section estimate for exp(Σz_iN_i)u. In particular h_z(γW_j,γW_j)=|Δ_j| is roughly monomial. This uses uniform near-identity comparison only after the least height is sufficiently large.
hypotheses: H.6 splitting-independent moving estimates and horizontal correction comparison.
The negative-Lie-chart correction is defined and analytic on the closed q-buffer.
proofSteps: Use H.6’s comparison between γu and exp(Σz_iN_i)u, with its depth and transverse-coordinate hypotheses.
Use gram-determinant-formulas to show fraction-algebra membership for the moving diagonal.
For determinant vectors the adapted flag identifies the absolute B determinant with the positive Hodge determinant.

sources.locator: §4.4 Lemma 4.7(2), Lemma 4.10 and final paragraph, pp.931–932

acceptance: The estimate is stable under compatible changes of splitting because the H.6 supplier states that independence explicitly.
The set where yₙ is bounded while y₁ grows is not compact; it is handled by the positive-height theorem below.

nodes.title: Rough polynomiality of Hodge-form entries
nodes.statement: For all fixed u,v in V_C the function z↦h_z(u,v) is roughly polynomial on a sufficiently deep ordered sector. Here roughly polynomial means g/d with g in the restricted-analytic coefficient Laurent-polynomial algebra and d in that algebra, nowhere zero and roughly monomial, using the repaired LD.6 localization convention. No nonzero hypothesis on u,v is needed. Finite sums, real/imaginary parts and conjugation are allowed by the imported algebra.
hypotheses: Use the repaired denominator convention, not the overly broad printed fraction-field condition.
Apply all needed norm comparisons after a common finite maximum of their depth thresholds.
proofSteps: For homogeneous vectors use the Gram formula; its numerator is a coefficient Laurent polynomial.
By moving-norm-rough-monomial, Δ_{j−1}Δ_j is a coefficient polynomial roughly monomial in absolute value.
Sum over the finite Gram contributions and then over the homogeneous decompositions of u,v using the LD.6 ring laws.

sources.match: The source proof actually yields polynomial denominators with monomial size; this stronger representation makes the claimed ring laws valid.

acceptance: The zero entry belongs to the rough-polynomial ring.
In a constant Tate family the entry h(u,v)=u conjugate(v) is a constant coefficient.

nodes.title: The determinant bound for a weight-adapted rational basis
nodes.statement: Choose any rational basis e_i homogeneous for the H.6 simultaneous weight splitting J of V_Q. For b_z, the real symmetric restriction of h_z, there are C>1 and Y such that ∏_i b_z(e_i,e_i)<C det(b_z in e) on orderedSector(n,R,Y). Each centered monodromy weight filtration has total weight zero, so the product of all comparison monomials is one. The determinant is a fixed positive multiple of |det Q in e| and is constant along the period domain. The basis need not be integral and no fixed ordering of its diagonal norms is asserted.
hypotheses: Fixed finite rank polarized pure variation, rational splitting J and fixed ordered rational basis.
H.3 faithful derived representation has determinant one; pure Hodge numbers are fixed.
proofSteps: Use flat-norm-rough-monomial for each of the finitely many basis vectors.
The centered weight multiset is symmetric by monodromy polarization, hence its total is zero at every partial filtration.
The Weil operator has fixed determinant on the component; thus det b is fixed and nonzero. Take C strictly larger than the product bound divided by this determinant.

sources.match: The determinant condition is independent of diagonal ordering and survives rational, rather than integral, basis choices.

acceptance: In rank two with weights +1 and −1, the diagonal comparison product is constant.
The same two diagonal entries can exchange order in more than one variable.

nodes.title: Reducedness along rational degeneration curves
nodes.statement: On every source curve used in the corrected LD.6 curve lemma—positive rational slopes among any initial block of degeneration coordinates, real intercepts, and the other coordinates fixed—the real Hodge form satisfies |b_z(e_i,e_j)|≤C_τ b_z(e_i,e_i) for the fixed rational weight-adapted basis e. sourceIssues.printed: The rough-polynomial definition permits fraction-field denominators of monomial size and then asserts closure under addition.
sourceIssues.correction: Require the denominator h to be a roughly monomial element of O[x,y,y^(−1)] (complex coefficients allowed for complex-valued functions). Then g/h + g'/h' = (gh' + g'h)/(hh') stays in the class, so T_n is a ring. In the proof of Lemma 4.7(3), write (4.4) over the denominator B(γ w_det K^(i−1))·B(γ w_det K^i), which lies in O_C[y] and is roughly monomial up to a constant phase by part (2), instead of dividing by the ratio (4.2).
sourceIssues.reason: As printed, h may be any roughly monomial element of O(x,y), and the sum of two roughly polynomial functions need not be roughly polynomial. Counterexample on Σ_1: let c = (x−1/2)² + y^(−2) ∈ O[x,y,y^(−1)] and k = (c + y^(−1))/(c + 2y^(−1)) ∈ (1/2, 1), so k ∼ 1. Then 1/k (g = 1, h = k) and −1 are roughly polynomial, but 1/k − 1 = y^(−1)/(c + y^(−1)) is not. Suppose it equals g/h with h ∼ y^s. Then g = h/(yc + 1). Write g = P(x,y) + O(y^A e^(−2πy)) with P ∈ R[x,y,y^(−1)], since the coefficients in O are analytic in q with |q| = e^(−2πy). For fixed x ≠ 1/2, |g| ≪ y^(s−1), so every y^j-coefficient of P with j ≥ s vanishes at every x ≠ 1/2, hence identically. But at x = 1/2, g ≫ y^s, a contradiction. The ring property is used in passing from Lemma 4.7 to Proposition 4.6 by sums over I-components and in h(u,v) = Σ_i h(ũ_i,ṽ_i). Both hold with the repaired definition. The author copy is identical, and the erratum is silent.

Hence ι∘Φ̃(Σ_n) ⊂ ∪_{σ∈S_m} T_{σe,C′}, a union of m! reduced sets with m = dim V. The curve statement should read: along each curve τ, h_z satisfies (1) (and (3)) for e with a constant C_τ.
sourceIssues.reason: Use the weight-three variation H¹(t₁)⊗Sym²H¹(t₂) of two Tate-curve families. Its six squared norm monomials in a fixed adapted basis have exponents y₁^s y₂^b, s∈{−1,1}, b∈{−2,0,2}. On (Y,Y), the three low directions are (−1,−2),(−1,0),(1,−2); on (Y³,Y), they are (−1,−2),(−1,0),(−1,2). Their intersection has dimension two. Uniform reducedness in one fixed ordered rational basis, using its ordering and determinant-product bounds and successive-minima comparison, would force its first three independent vectors into both low subspaces. This is impossible. Sorting finitely many basis orderings repairs the Claim while preserving the finite-Siegel conclusion. The one-variable bound used for off-diagonal transfer is retained without a fixed-order assertion.
